summary: The note describes tetanic contraction, a sustained muscle contraction produced when a motor nerve fires action potentials at a very high rate, so that twitches overlap and the motor unit stays maximally stimulated. It distinguishes unfused (incomplete) from fused (complete) tetanus and explains that tetanic activity ranges from normal voluntary holding and healthy muscle tone to pathologic involuntary conditions such as dystonia and pathologic tetanus.
one_line: Describes tetanic contraction, a sustained high-frequency muscle contraction that ranges from normal posture and muscle tone to pathologic involuntary disorders.
key_facts: A tetanic contraction is a sustained muscle contraction evoked when the motor nerve that innervates a skeletal muscle emits action potentials at a very high rate.
Tetanic contraction is also called tetanized state, tetanus, or physiologic tetanus, the latter to differentiate it from the disease called tetanus.
If stimuli are delivered slowly enough, the tension in the muscle relaxes between successive twitches.
If stimuli are delivered at high frequency, the twitches overlap, resulting in tetanic contraction.
An unfused tetanus occurs when the muscle fibers do not completely relax before the next stimulus, though there is partial relaxation between twitches.
Fused tetanus occurs when there is no relaxation of the muscle fibers between stimuli, during a high rate of stimulation.
A fused tetanic contraction is the strongest single-unit twitch in contraction.
When tetanized, the contracting tension in the muscle remains constant in a steady state, which is the maximal possible contraction.
Lifting a heavy box off the floor is isotonic, but holding it at the elevated position is isometric.
Isotonic contractions place muscles in a constant tension but the muscle length changes, while isometric contractions hold a constant muscle length.
Muscle tone is a healthy form of involuntary sustained partial contraction.
Healthy muscle tone differs from isometric tetanic contraction only in the percentage of motor units participating at any moment and the frequency of neural signals.
Involuntary sustained contraction of a hypertonic type is a pathologic process.
On the mild part of the spectrum are cramps, spasms, and even tetany, which are often temporary and nonsevere.
On the moderate to severe parts of the spectrum are dystonia, trismus, pathologic tetanus, and other movement disorders featuring involuntary sustained strong contractions of skeletal muscle.

entities.name: Tetanus
entities.role: disease that the term physiologic tetanus is used to differentiate from tetanic contraction

entities.name: Unfused tetanus
entities.role: incomplete tetanic contraction in which muscle fibers partially relax between twitches

entities.name: Fused tetanus
entities.role: complete tetanic contraction with no relaxation of muscle fibers between stimuli

entities.name: Muscle tone
entities.role: healthy form of involuntary sustained partial contraction that maintains posture

entities.name: Isotonic contraction
entities.role: contraction type with constant tension and changing muscle length, such as lifting a heavy box

entities.name: Isometric contraction
entities.role: contraction type with constant muscle length, such as holding a heavy box at an elevated position

entities.role: movement disorder featuring involuntary sustained strong contractions of skeletal muscle on the moderate to severe part of the spectrum
